summary: 3. The Commission, after considering the application of the Petitioner in light of the provisions of the Act and the Transmission Licence Regulations, in its order dated 24.5.2025, prima facie proposed to grant a transmission licence to the Petitioner. The relevant extracts of the order dated 24.5.2025 are extracted as under: 5. The matter was called out for hearing on 5.6.2025. During the course of the hearing, the Commission noted that the Office of the Commission had received a suggestion/objection dated 22.5.2025 from Ms. Alpa Patel and Mr. Prakash Patel in the present matter. Accordingly, the Petitioner was directed to obtain a copy of the said suggestion/objection from the Office of the Commission, if not already received, and to file its response, if any, within two weeks. Accordingly, the matter was reserved for the Order. 6. Ms. Alpa Priyankant Patel and Mr. Prakash Ishwarbhai Patel in their counter affidavits dated 22.5.2025, have reiterated their earlier submissions and denied the claims made by the Petitioner in its reply dated 12.4.2025. The main contentions raised in the counter affidavits are as under: - c) The Petitioner has made a false claim regarding the objection being time-barred. Since the notice under Section 68 of the Electricity Act, 2003 was served on 18.2.2025, the Objector maintains that they are well within their legal right to submit objections whether in writing or orally. - d) The Petitioner is misleading the Commission by citing the approval under Section 68 of Electricity Act, 2003 without disclosing its conditional nature. The transmission lines are being laid without providing a detailed route map or revenue survey details, despite RTI application and legal notices addressed to the Petitioner, CEA and the Ministry of Power. - f) The public notice dated 25.10.2024, published by the Petitioner, was general in nature and did not include crucial details such as revenue survey numbers of lands of a particular village, taluka and district through which line is passing. Thus, filling objection by present objector or any citizen does not arise. Also, since the aforesaid notice did not contain any details of survey number / village / taluka / district, the question of giving objections at relevant time does not arise. In this regard, the objector has placed reliance on certain judicial pronouncements to substantiate their submissions. - j) Since, the Petitioner commenced excavation work prior to the expiry of the objection submission deadline, i.e., before 5.4.2025, it did not provide the objector opportunity to file objections. The permission of the cultivator, and not the landowner, was taken by the Petitioner. The Collector, Vadodara, transferred the legal notice of the objector to the Collector of Khambhat, who held no jurisdiction in this case. Further, the objector also submitted that references to compensation are irrelevant, as no such prayer was made by the objector. - k) The Petitioner’s claim of potential project delay is an attempt to pressure the Commission and deflect scrutiny. The contract was awarded to a newly incorporated SPV of PFC Ltd. without due process or a proper route map, etc. - m) The Petitioner acted as a silent spectator despite having received the written request of the objector dated 19.3.2025 regarding want of details of survey, approvals under Sections 68 and 164. 7. In response to the above objections, the Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 11.7.2025, has submitted as under: - a) The objections raised are barred by the doctrine of _res judicata_ , as embodied in Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, which prohibits re-litigation of issues already adjudicated upon between the same parties. The Commission has already addressed similar issues in its earlier order dated 24.5.2025. Entertaining the same issue once again would not only lead to multiplicity of proceedings but also delay the implementation of the project. Accordingly, the counter affidavit dated 22.5.2025 is deserves to be dismissed at the outset, as the matters raised therein have already been conclusively decided by the Commission in its order dated 24.5.2025. - g) The objectors’ claims of non-disclosure or procedural irregularities are unfounded, as the Petitioner has ensured transparency and adequate stakeholder access throughout the process. - h) The Petitioner has addressed the grievance of Mr. Prakash I. Patel vide letter dated 5.4.2025, wherein it was clarified that the concerned transmission line does not pass through Village Raval, Taluka Vaghodiya, District Vadodara, where the objector claimed ownership of land. Further, the copy of the Section 68 approval, as requested by Mr. Prakash I. Patel, was duly provided. 10. In our order dated 24.5.2025, we had proposed to grant a transmission licence to the Petitioner company and directed the issue of public notice. In response to the Regulations or any other regulation of the Commission or as per the directions of the Commission as may be issued from time to time; 13. It is expected that while carrying out the survey, the Petitioner has complied with the provisions of clauses 2.5.7.3, 2.5.7.4, and 2.5.7.5 of the RfP. The Petitioner will comply with the provisions of the bidding documents and the TSA for the commissioning of the Project within the SCOD in letter and spirit. 14. An extract copy of this order be sent to CTUIL, CEA, and BPC for information and necessary action.
title: Application under Sections 14 & 15 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for Grant of Transmission License and other related matters) Regulations, 2024 with respect to grant of Transmission License to South Olpad Transmission Limited. POWERGRID South Olpad Transmission Limited
